title: Abgoosht
subtitle: lamb and chickpea broth
excerpt: Abgoosht is a thick Persian lamb and chickpea broth traditionally served in two courses: first the strained broth poured over bread, then the mashed solids eaten with raw herbs and flatbread. Serves 4.
sourceNotes: Abgoosht, literally meaning meat water, is one of Iran's oldest peasant dishes. It was traditionally cooked slowly in a stone pot called a dizi, giving the dish an alternative name.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze broth and mashed solids separately for up to 3 months.

glossaryTerms.definition: Literally 'meat water' in Persian, a thick lamb and legume broth traditionally eaten in two courses: the strained soup first, then the mashed solids.
The stone or clay pot in which abgoosht is traditionally cooked and served, giving the dish one of its common names.

. The technique of serving the broth first and then mashing the solids for a second course is unique to this dish. Three hours of slow cooking is what makes it work. Serves 4.
Use the pestle and mortar to mash the strained solids at the table for the second course. Serve with flatbread, raw onion, fresh herbs and pickles.

items.prepNote: soaked overnight in cold water, drained

content.text: Place the lamb, drained chickpeas, onion, tinned tomatoes, turmeric, cinnamon stick, dried chilli and water into the stockpot. Bring to a boil over high heat. Skim off any foam that rises to the surface in the first 10 minutes.

Reduce heat to very low. Cover and simmer for 2 hours. After 2 hours, add the potatoes to the pot. Cover and continue cooking for a further 1 hour until the lamb falls off the bone and the chickpeas are completely soft.
Remove the lamb bones and the cinnamon stick from the pot. Use a slotted spoon or ladle to scoop all the solid ingredients into a large bowl, leaving the broth behind in the pot.
Serve the first course: ladle the hot broth into bowls. Tear flatbread into chunks, place in each bowl and pour the broth over. Eat this soup course first.

For the second course, use the pestle and mortar to mash the lamb, potato and chickpea solids to a rough paste. Add a ladle of broth to loosen. Serve the mash with flatbread, raw sliced onion, fresh herbs and torshi pickles if you have them.

attrs.solution: Always soak dried chickpeas overnight. If still firm after the full cook time, continue for another 30 to 45 minutes. Old dried chickpeas take longer. Tinned chickpeas added in the last hour are a workable substitute.
Skim the surface during the first 30 minutes of cooking and again after refrigerating overnight. The fat solidifies and lifts off cleanly when cold.
Add broth a ladle at a time until the mash is spreadable. It should have the consistency of thick hummus, not dry mashed potato.

content.text: Abgoosht is Iran's oldest everyday dish. It was the food of labourers, shepherds and working families for centuries. Traditional dizi restaurants in Tehran still serve it in individual stone pots at the table. Each diner gets their own pot, strains the broth themselves and mashes their own solids. It is a deeply social, unhurried meal.
